problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\frac{2}{t},$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t={e}^{3}\,\text{s}$, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary. Do not round your answer.

The particle is stationary at $t=$
{{field-1}}$\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{2}{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v({e}^{3})=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})+C \\ 4 & =6+C \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)-2.$ 

Now, we find the moments in time when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)-2 & =0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(t) & =1 \\ t & =e.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particle is stationary when $t=e\,\text{s}.$
